correctness.rationale: Same-part selected pairs are the only nonadjacent selected pairs. They are visible exactly when an omitted vertex exists outside their part. For a nonempty complement of size t, nonvisibility therefore means that the complement lies in one part of size at least t+2, giving a disjoint binomial subtraction. The maximum class, unique cubic minimizer, near-top coefficient, and N=6 threshold follow exactly. Definition-level exhaustive checks independently confirm the criterion and every coefficient through order ten.

originality.rationale: Published work covers complete-bipartite visibility polynomials, a general two-graph join recurrence, complete-multipartite maximum mutual-visibility numbers, and several other explicit graph-class polynomials. Those are acknowledged as prior coverage of the counting machinery and optimization special cases. The inspected sources do not state the fixed-order coefficientwise extremal classification or the exact failure-of-minimum threshold.
residual_risks: The general join recurrence makes the complete-multipartite coefficient formula derivable with additional specialization; only the cross-partition extremal theorem is asserted as original.

The coefficientwise maximum can be attained by several nonisomorphic multipartite graphs; the theorem classifies all of them rather than claiming uniqueness.

value.rationale: Visibility polynomials were introduced specifically to retain all-size information lost by the maximum mutual-visibility number. Within a canonical graph family, coefficientwise extremality is therefore a natural structural question. The theorem gives all maximizers and a sharp phase change at order six where minimization becomes impossible, with an infinite crossing family rather than a one-off example.
